tomato.when: September to December; again in January for autumn.
tomato.tip: Fruit fly is the main battle from December; early plantings crop before it peaks.

cherry-tomato.suit: Grows very well; handles humidity better than big tomatoes.
cherry-tomato.tip: Often self-seeds here and pops up again each spring.

capsicum.tip: Needs a warm, sheltered spot to set fruit; north-facing walls help.

eggplant.suit: Grows well in a hot spot.
eggplant.tip: Slow to start in cool springs; wait until soil feels warm to the touch.

zucchini.tip: Powdery mildew arrives with late-summer humidity; sow a second crop in January.

cucumber.tip: Lebanese types cope best with coastal humidity.

pumpkin.tip: Plant early so pumpkins ripen before autumn rain causes rot.

bush-beans.tip: Sow every 4 weeks; bean fly can hit summer sowings.

climbing-beans.tip: Scarlet runners can come back for a second year in frost-free spots.

sweet-corn.tip: Possums love ripening cobs; cover them with bags.

sweet-potato.tip: Coastal sands grow smooth tubers; dig before winter rains.

chilli-bell-lantern.tip: Overwinters on the coast and crops earlier in its second year.

chilli-long-red.tip: Often crops into June in frost-free gardens.

basil.tip: Dies with the first cool nights in May; take cuttings indoors.

thai-basil.tip: Tougher than sweet basil in humid February weather.

sunflower.tip: Stake tall types against summer storms.

marigold.tip: Plant among tomatoes to draw beneficial insects.

toothache-plant.tip: Can carry on through mild coastal winters in a sheltered spot.

broccoli.tip: Plant by April for heads before the coldest weeks.

cabbage.tip: Net early; cabbage whites are active until May.

cauliflower.tip: Warm autumns can cause small, loose heads; plant on time.

kale.tip: Keeps cropping into November before aphids take over.

english-spinach.tip: Bolts by October; switch to silverbeet for summer.

peas.tip: Sow after the soil cools in March; mildew ends crops in spring.

snow-peas.tip: One of the most reliable winter crops on the coast.

bok-choy.tip: Ready in 6 weeks; sow small batches.

coriander.suit: Grows well in the cool months.
coriander.tip: Bolts within weeks in summer; grow Vietnamese mint instead.

dill.when: March to May and August to September.
dill.tip: Dislikes summer humidity; best as a spring and autumn crop.

sweet-pea.when: March to April (St Patrick's Day is traditional).
sweet-pea.tip: Flowers August to November; add lime to sandy soil.

onion.tip: Long-day varieties won't bulb this far north; check the label.

garlic.tip: Use Australian-grown softneck garlic; supermarket bulbs often fail.

leek.tip: Hill up soil in winter for long white stems.

potato.tip: Avoid harvesting in wet weather to stop rot.

calendula.tip: Flowers through winter and self-seeds for next year.

lettuce.when: All year; heat-tolerant types in summer.
lettuce.tip: Grow summer lettuce under afternoon shade.

rocket.tip: Sharper and quicker to bolt in summer.

carrot.when: All year; best February to October.
carrot.tip: Sandy coastal soils grow long, straight roots.

beetroot.tip: Slow in midwinter; sow from late winter.

radish.tip: Ready in 4 weeks; sow little and often.

silverbeet.tip: One of the most reliable greens in coastal heat.

spring-onion.tip: Regrows from the root ends after cutting.

parsley.when: All year; easiest in spring and autumn.
parsley.tip: Usually lasts about 18 months before going to seed.

nasturtium.tip: Pull extra seedlings before they smother small plants.

apple.tip: Choose 'Anna', 'Dorsett Golden' or 'Tropic Sweet'; plant two for pollination.

peach.tip: 'Tropic Snow' and 'Florida Prince' fruit before fruit fly peaks.

raspberry.tip: 'Heritage' crops on new canes and suits mild winters.

rhubarb.tip: Stems stay greener in warm winters; flavour is still good.

asparagus.tip: Spears come in August to October in mild winters.

hops.tip: Grows as a summer screen but rarely gives big cone crops this far north.

rosemary.tip: Handles salt wind; perfect for sandy coastal soil.

thyme.tip: Plant in gritty soil or pots; summer humidity rots it in heavy soil.

oregano.tip: Flavour is strongest in dry, sunny spots.

sage.tip: Often dies in a wet February; keep cuttings as backup.

tarragon.suit: Grows; French tarragon struggles in humidity.
tarragon.tip: Russian tarragon grows more easily but has less flavour.

bay-tree.tip: Scale is common; wipe or spray with horticultural oil.

french-lavender.tip: Handles coastal humidity better than English lavender.

mint.tip: Keep in a pot; it spreads fast in moist soil.

chives.tip: May die back in summer heat and return in autumn.

self-heal.tip: Good groundcover in moist part shade.

valerian.tip: Afternoon shade helps it through summer.

comfrey.tip: Choose its spot carefully; it's almost impossible to remove.

echinacea-purpurea.suit: Grows; can rot in wet humid summers.
echinacea-purpurea.tip: Plant in free-draining soil or a raised bed.

avocado.tip: Root rot is the main killer; plant on a mound.

banana.tip: Fruit is slow to ripen in cooler winters; dwarf Cavendish is easiest.

passionfruit.tip: Grafted vines throw suckers; remove them promptly.

frangipani.tip: Keep dry in winter to avoid rot.

bougainvillea.suit: Grows well in hot, sunny spots.
bougainvillea.tip: Flowers most in sun with little water.

ginger.suit: Grows in warm, sheltered part shade.
ginger.tip: Dies back in winter; keep the soil dry then.

turmeric.suit: Grows in warm, sheltered part shade.
turmeric.tip: Harvest after leaves die back in late autumn.

lemongrass.tip: Cut back hard in late winter.

curry-leaf.tip: Suckers freely; keep it in check.

vietnamese-mint.tip: Loves wet spots; dies back in cold snaps.

lemon.tip: Meyer and Eureka fruit almost year-round here.

lime.tip: Tahitian lime crops best in a warm, sheltered spot.

orange.tip: Navels ripen in winter; Valencias in spring and summer.

mandarin.tip: Fruit fly attacks ripening fruit; pick promptly.

finger-lime.tip: Native to northern NSW rainforests; likes part shade.

strawberry.tip: Crops August to December; birds are the main pest.

fig.tip: Net fruit in late summer against birds and fruit fly.

feijoa.tip: Handles salt wind; good coastal hedge.

olive.tip: Fruits better in drier inland areas; still a good screen.

grape.tip: Choose mildew-resistant table grapes such as 'Isabella'.

camellia.tip: Sasanquas flower in autumn; japonicas in winter.

azalea.tip: Petal blight is common in humid springs.

gardenia.tip: Yellow leaves in winter usually recover in spring.

hydrangea.suit: Grows very well in part shade.
hydrangea.tip: Acidic Sydney soils give blue flowers.

blueberry.tip: Choose southern highbush or rabbiteye; use acidic potting mix in pots.

rose.tip: Black spot is common in humid summers; choose resistant varieties.

pelargonium.tip: Flowers nearly year-round on the coast.

agapanthus.tip: Deadhead; it can spread into bushland.

kangaroo-paw.tip: Choose hybrid types bred for the east coast.

lomandra.tip: Tough in sand, clay, sun or shade.

banksia.tip: Coast banksia and old man banksia are local natives.

warrigal-greens.tip: Native to NSW beaches; self-seeds in sand.

monstera.suit: Easy indoors; grows outdoors in shade.
monstera.tip: Can climb trees outdoors in frost-free gardens.

peace-lily.tip: Can grow outdoors in deep shade on the coast.

pothos.tip: Keep indoors; it can escape into bushland outdoors.

spider-plant.tip: Also makes a good shady groundcover outdoors.

rubber-plant.tip: Grows into a large tree if planted outdoors; keep it potted.

aloe-vera.suit: Grows indoors or outdoors in sun.
aloe-vera.tip: Grows outdoors year-round on the coast.

boston-fern.suit: Grows indoors or on shady verandahs.

moth-orchid.tip: Flowers mainly in late winter and spring.

tomato.suit: Grows well in spring and autumn; struggles in midsummer.
tomato.when: August to September, and February to March.
tomato.tip: Autumn plantings dodge the worst fruit fly and summer disease.

cherry-tomato.suit: Grows very well; the most reliable tomato here.
cherry-tomato.when: August to October, and February to March.
cherry-tomato.tip: Small fruit ripens fast enough to beat most fruit fly.

capsicum.tip: Crops well into winter in frost-free gardens.

eggplant.suit: Grows very well; loves the heat.
eggplant.tip: One of the few fruiting crops that handles midsummer here.

zucchini.when: August to September, and February to March.
zucchini.tip: Summer crops collapse with mildew and fruit rot; avoid December plantings.

cucumber.tip: Grow up a trellis to keep fruit off wet ground.

pumpkin.when: August to October, and January to February.
pumpkin.tip: Pumpkin beetle and mildew are heavy; Queensland Blue copes well.

bush-beans.when: August to October, and February to April.
bush-beans.tip: Bean fly is bad in summer; autumn sowings crop best.

climbing-beans.when: August to September, and February to March.
climbing-beans.tip: Snake beans are a better choice for summer here.

sweet-corn.tip: Corn earworm is common; check silks and remove grubs.

sweet-potato.tip: Thrives in the heat; often crops year-round.

chilli-bell-lantern.tip: Fruit fly attacks soft ripe fruit; bag clusters.

chilli-long-red.tip: Can crop for several years without frost.

basil.tip: Often lives through winter; replace when woody.

thai-basil.tip: Handles summer humidity better than sweet basil.

sunflower.tip: Storms flatten tall types; choose dwarf or stake well.

marigold.tip: Spider mites flare in dry spring heat.

toothache-plant.tip: Thrives in the warm, humid summers.

broccoli.tip: Choose quick, heat-tolerant varieties for early plantings.

cabbage.tip: Mini cabbages mature before spring heat.

cauliflower.suit: Hard: needs cool nights to head.
cauliflower.tip: Choose fast, subtropical varieties and plant on time.

kale.tip: Aphids explode in spring; pull plants by October.

english-spinach.tip: Grow Warrigal greens or Brazilian spinach for the rest of the year.

peas.tip: Sow once days cool; mildew ends crops by September.

snow-peas.tip: Very reliable through the dry, sunny winter.

bok-choy.tip: Bolts fast once spring warms up.

coriander.tip: Bolts as soon as days warm; grow Vietnamese mint in summer.

sweet-pea.tip: Choose early-flowering varieties to beat spring heat.

onion.tip: Only short-day varieties bulb here; harvest by November.

garlic.tip: Refrigerate cloves for 4–6 weeks before planting to help them bulb.

potato.when: July to August, and February to March.
potato.tip: Late-winter plantings crop before summer heat.

lettuce.when: March to October; heat-tolerant types in summer.
lettuce.tip: Summer lettuce needs shade cloth and daily water.

rocket.suit: Grows best in the cool months.

carrot.tip: Summer sowings germinate poorly in hot soil.

beetroot.tip: Leaves get leaf spot in humid weather.

radish.suit: Grows best in the cool months.
radish.tip: Gets hot and woody in summer.

silverbeet.tip: Leaf spot in summer; remove affected leaves.

parsley.suit: Grows best in the cool months.
parsley.tip: Often dies in summer wet season.

nasturtium.suit: Grows well in the cool months.

apple.tip: Only very low-chill types such as 'Anna' or 'Tropic Sweet' fruit.

peach.tip: 'Tropic Snow' and 'FlordaPrince'; fruit fly is a major problem.

raspberry.tip: Try native raspberries or 'Heritage'; humidity brings disease.

rhubarb.tip: Grow as a winter crop in a pot with excellent drainage.

hops.tip: Needs long summer days and winter cold.

rosemary.tip: Plant in a raised bed; wet summers rot it in clay.

thyme.tip: Often rots in the wet season; grow in pots and keep dry.

oregano.tip: Greek oregano copes best with humidity.

sage.tip: Grow in a pot in full sun; replace yearly.

tarragon.tip: Grow Mexican tarragon (Tagetes lucida) instead; it loves the heat.

bay-tree.tip: Watch for scale in humid weather.

french-lavender.tip: The best lavender for subtropical gardens.

yarrow-white.tip: Cut back after flowering to stop rot in wet weather.

mint.tip: Rust appears in humid summers; cut back hard.

chives.tip: Often sulks in summer; garlic chives are tougher.

valerian.tip: Often short-lived; grow in afternoon shade.

comfrey.tip: Dies back in heat but returns.

echinacea-purpurea.tip: Grow in a raised bed or pot with gritty mix.

avocado.tip: Choose Hass with a pollinator such as Bacon; plant on a mound.

banana.tip: Check Queensland rules: you may need a permit to plant bananas.

passionfruit.tip: Passionvine hopper and fruit fly are common.

frangipani.tip: Rust shows in humid autumns but rarely harms the tree.

bougainvillea.tip: Prune hard after flowering to control size.

ginger.tip: A classic SEQ crop; harvest young ginger from February.

turmeric.tip: Harvest in June when leaves die back.

lemongrass.tip: Divide clumps every couple of years.

vietnamese-mint.tip: The perfect summer replacement for coriander.

lemon.tip: Lemonade (a lemon-mandarin cross) is popular here.

orange.tip: Navels can be dry; Valencias suit the climate.

strawberry.tip: Plant new runners each autumn; summer heat kills them.

fig.suit: Grows; rust and fruit fly are problems.
fig.tip: Bag fruit; choose 'Brown Turkey' or 'Black Genoa'.

feijoa.suit: Grows; fruit fly can attack fruit.
feijoa.tip: Use fruit fly traps in autumn.

olive.tip: Grow mainly as an ornamental screen.

grape.tip: Choose disease-resistant types such as 'Isabella' or 'Flame Seedless'.

mulberry.tip: Dwarf types crop on and off most of the year.

camellia.tip: Sasanquas cope better with heat than japonicas.

azalea.tip: Lace bug is common in dry winters.

hydrangea.tip: Wilts in hot afternoons; water deeply.

blueberry.tip: Rabbiteye and southern highbush types such as 'Biloxi' suit SEQ.

rose.tip: Choose disease-resistant roses and prune to open the centre.

pelargonium.tip: Wet summers rot them; grow in pots under eaves.

salvia.tip: Many salvias love the subtropical warmth.

grevillea.tip: Local hybrids such as 'Superb' suit the climate.

kangaroo-paw.tip: Grow hybrid types in pots with gritty mix.

lilly-pilly.tip: Native to the region; choose psyllid-resistant types.

banksia.tip: Coast banksia and wallum banksia suit sandy coastal soils.

correa.tip: Needs good drainage in wet summers.

monstera.tip: Can become weedy outdoors; keep it contained.

peace-lily.suit: Grows indoors or in outdoor shade.

pothos.tip: Keep indoors; it climbs and spreads in local bushland.

snake-plant.tip: Can be weedy outdoors in Queensland; keep it potted.

fiddle-leaf-fig.suit: Grows indoors or outdoors in shade.
fiddle-leaf-fig.tip: Can grow into a tree outdoors; keep it potted.

spider-plant.tip: Grows outdoors as a shady groundcover.

rubber-plant.tip: Grows into a huge tree outdoors; keep potted.

aloe-vera.tip: Keep dry in the wet season.

boston-fern.suit: Grows indoors or outdoors in shade.

moth-orchid.tip: Can grow outdoors on a tree in sheltered shade.

tomato.suit: Grows in the dry season only.
tomato.tip: Choose heat-set and disease-resistant varieties; cherry types are most reliable.

cherry-tomato.suit: Grows well in the dry season.
cherry-tomato.tip: The best tomato for the tropics.

capsicum.tip: Crops until the build-up heat in October.

eggplant.suit: Grows very well; can last into the wet.
eggplant.tip: Long Asian types handle the heat best.

zucchini.suit: Grows in the dry season only.
zucchini.tip: Hand-pollinate early in the morning; bees are scarce in some areas.

cucumber.tip: Apple cucumbers cope best with heat.

pumpkin.tip: Trombone squash (rampicante) resists pests better than true pumpkins.

bush-beans.tip: Snake beans and winged beans grow through the wet instead.

climbing-beans.tip: Grow snake beans for wet-season crops.

sweet-corn.tip: Needs daily water in the dry.

sweet-potato.when: Any time, best at the start of the wet.
sweet-potato.tip: Leaves are a great wet-season green.

chilli-bell-lantern.tip: Bird's eye and other chillies thrive here year-round.

basil.suit: Grows in the dry season; struggles in the wet.
basil.tip: Thai and holy basil cope with the wet season better.

sunflower.tip: Storms flatten tall types; plant dwarf varieties.

toothache-plant.tip: Native to tropical America; thrives here.

broccoli.tip: Choose sprouting types and plant in the coolest weeks.

cabbage.tip: Chinese cabbage is more reliable than round cabbage.

cauliflower.tip: Rarely forms heads without cool nights.

kale.tip: Collards and Asian greens are easier.

english-spinach.tip: Grow Ceylon spinach, kangkong or Warrigal greens instead.

peas.tip: Snow peas do better than shelling peas.

snow-peas.tip: Sow in the coolest weeks for a short crop.

bok-choy.tip: Quick and reliable; ready in 5–6 weeks.

coriander.tip: Bolts fast; grow Vietnamese coriander or culantro year-round.

sweet-pea.tip: Short flowering in the coolest weeks only.

onion.tip: Grow spring onions and shallots instead; they're far easier.

garlic.tip: Bulbs rarely form; grow garlic chives instead.

leek.tip: Grows quickly; harvest before the wet.

potato.tip: Plant certified seed potatoes; tubers rot in wet soil.

calendula.tip: Dies off in the build-up heat.

lettuce.tip: Shade cloth and daily water are essential.

carrot.tip: Short varieties suit hard or sandy soils.

beetroot.tip: Water evenly to stop woody roots.

silverbeet.suit: Grows in the dry season; can survive the wet.
silverbeet.tip: Ceylon spinach is better for the wet season.

celery.tip: Needs constant water; grow in shade.

spring-onion.tip: One of the easiest crops in the tropics.

apple.tip: Try tropical fruit such as mango, lychee or star apple instead.

peach.tip: Even low-chill types rarely fruit here.

raspberry.tip: Try native or Atherton raspberries in Far North Queensland highlands.

rhubarb.tip: Rots in the wet season; rosella stems make a tart substitute.

asparagus.tip: Spears don't form without a cool rest period.

hops.tip: Needs long summer days and cold winters.

rosemary.tip: Grow in a pot of gritty mix and keep it out of monsoon rain.

thyme.tip: Treat as a dry-season annual in pots.

oregano.tip: Cuban oregano (a succulent) thrives here instead.

sage.tip: Usually dies in the wet season.

bay-tree.tip: Grows slowly in the heat; keep in part shade.

french-lavender.tip: Grow in a pot under cover during the wet.

mint.tip: Vietnamese mint is more reliable in the wet.

chives.tip: Garlic chives are much easier here.

comfrey.tip: Dies back in the build-up; returns with water.

avocado.tip: Hass struggles here; ask a local nursery for tropical (West Indian) types and plant on a mound.

banana.tip: Check local biosecurity rules; permits may be required to plant bananas.

passionfruit.tip: Panama and yellow passionfruit cope best with humidity.

frangipani.tip: Flowers for most of the year.

bougainvillea.tip: Flowers best in the dry season.

ginger.tip: Harvest when leaves die back in the dry.

lemongrass.tip: Thrives in the heat and rain.

lemon.tip: Lemonade and Meyer types do best.

lime.tip: Tahitian and kaffir limes are the best citrus for the tropics.

orange.tip: Green-skinned oranges can still be sweet and ripe.

mandarin.tip: Taste-test rather than wait for orange skin.

finger-lime.tip: Needs shade from harsh dry-season sun.

strawberry.tip: Plant runners each April; they die in the wet.

fig.tip: Grows, but fruit often splits or rots in the wet.

feijoa.tip: Needs some cold to fruit well.

olive.tip: Needs dry summers and cool winters.

grape.tip: Only tropical varieties fruit; mildew is heavy.

mulberry.tip: One of the few berries that thrives in the tropics.

camellia.tip: Needs shade and acidic mix; often struggles.

azalea.tip: Rarely thrives; grow ixora for a similar look.

gardenia.tip: The best of the acid-lovers for the tropics.

hydrangea.tip: Needs deep shade and lots of water.

blueberry.tip: Only very low-chill types in pots; often disappointing.

rose.tip: Some old Chinese and tropical roses cope; black spot is severe.

pelargonium.tip: Rots in the wet season; keep pots under cover.

salvia.tip: Tropical salvias such as Salvia leucantha cope best.

agapanthus.tip: Grows but flowers poorly in the heat.

grevillea.tip: Northern species and hybrids such as 'Honey Gem' thrive.

bottlebrush.tip: Tropical weeping bottlebrushes suit the climate.

lilly-pilly.tip: Many tropical lilly pillies are local natives.

westringia.tip: Needs good drainage in the wet.

banksia.tip: Banksia dentata is the tropical banksia.

correa.tip: A southern plant that struggles in the heat.

warrigal-greens.tip: Kangkong is better for the wet season.

monstera.tip: Can be invasive outdoors; keep it contained.

pothos.tip: A declared weed risk in some northern areas; keep in pots.

snake-plant.tip: Can spread into bushland; keep it potted.

rubber-plant.tip: Becomes a huge tree with invasive roots; keep potted.

moth-orchid.suit: Grows outdoors on trees in shade.
moth-orchid.tip: Mount on a tree trunk in dappled shade.

tomato.tip: Plant by October so fruit sets before the hottest weeks; Medfly is the main pest.

cherry-tomato.tip: Copes with Perth heat better than large tomatoes.

capsicum.tip: Fruit sunburns in January heat; keep leaf cover and use shade cloth.

eggplant.suit: Grows very well; loves the heat.
eggplant.tip: Thrives in Perth's long, hot summers.

zucchini.tip: Water at the base; powdery mildew appears in autumn.

cucumber.tip: Mulch thickly; dry sand makes fruit bitter.

pumpkin.tip: Grow over a pile of compost; sand alone holds too little water.

bush-beans.tip: Beans wilt on 40°C days; water the evening before.

climbing-beans.tip: Plant against an east-facing fence to avoid afternoon heat.

sweet-corn.tip: Needs lots of water; drippers under mulch work best on rostered days.

sweet-potato.tip: Perth's sand grows smooth, clean tubers.

chilli-bell-lantern.tip: Can overwinter in sheltered coastal suburbs.

chilli-long-red.tip: Medfly attacks ripe fruit; pick promptly.

basil.tip: Needs afternoon shade on the hottest days.

thai-basil.tip: Handles the heat better than sweet basil.

marigold.tip: Good companion for tomatoes against nematodes in sand.

toothache-plant.tip: Wilts fast in dry sand; mulch and water daily in summer.

broccoli.tip: Plant as soon as March cools; heads form through winter.

cabbage.tip: Winter rain does much of the watering.

cauliflower.tip: Needs rich soil; dig in plenty of compost.

kale.tip: Crops right through the wet winter.

english-spinach.tip: Bolts by October as days lengthen.

peas.tip: Winter rain suits them; sow after the first autumn rains.

bok-choy.tip: Ready in 6 weeks; sow small batches.

dill.when: March to May and August to September.

sweet-pea.tip: Flowers through late winter and spring.

onion.tip: Short- and intermediate-day varieties suit Perth.

garlic.tip: Harvest in November before the soil gets hot.

leek.tip: Hill up sand around stems for long white shanks.

potato.tip: Perth's sand grows clean potatoes; a classic WA crop.

lettuce.suit: Grows year-round with shade in summer.
lettuce.when: All year; easiest March to October.
lettuce.tip: Use shade cloth and water daily in summer.

carrot.when: All year; best February to October.

beetroot.tip: Keep moist; dry sand makes woody roots.

radish.when: All year; best in the cool months.

silverbeet.tip: One of the easiest crops in Perth.

celery.tip: Hard in sand; grow in a wicking bed.

parsley.tip: Needs shade and water in summer.

apple.tip: Choose low-chill types for the coast; the Perth Hills and south-west grow classic apples.

peach.tip: Medfly attacks ripe fruit; net or bag.

raspberry.tip: Better in the Perth Hills and south-west; needs constant water.

rhubarb.suit: Grows with water and afternoon shade.
rhubarb.tip: Summer heat can collapse plants; mulch heavily.

asparagus.tip: Sandy soil suits it; feed generously.

hops.tip: Better in cooler areas such as Margaret River and Albany.

rosemary.tip: A perfect plant for Perth's climate and sand.

oregano.tip: Flavour is excellent in Perth's sun.

sage.tip: Dry summers suit it far better than the humid east coast.

tarragon.tip: French tarragon does better here than in humid climates.

bay-tree.tip: Shelter young plants from hot easterlies.

mint.tip: Needs daily water in summer; best in a pot with a saucer.

self-heal.tip: Needs moist soil; hard in dry sand.

valerian.tip: Needs shade, rich soil and constant moisture.

comfrey.tip: Deep roots cope with dry summers.

avocado.tip: Needs lots of water and protection from hot easterlies; plant in a sheltered spot.

banana.tip: Check Department of Agriculture rules before planting; needs constant water.

passionfruit.tip: Water deeply; a Perth backyard classic.

bougainvillea.tip: Thrives in heat with little water.

ginger.tip: Needs constant moisture; grow in a pot.

turmeric.tip: Grow in a pot with rich mix.

curry-leaf.tip: Protect from frost in outer suburbs.

vietnamese-mint.tip: Keep the pot in a saucer of water.

lemon.tip: Feed little and often; nutrients wash out of sand.

orange.tip: Medfly attacks ripe fruit; use traps.

finger-lime.tip: Needs shelter from hot afternoon sun.

strawberry.tip: Crops through spring; protect from Medfly and birds.

olive.tip: Can become weedy in bushland; harvest or remove fallen fruit.

camellia.tip: Grow in pots of acidic mix in shade; bore water can yellow leaves.

azalea.tip: Grow in pots in shade; alkaline water causes problems.

gardenia.tip: Needs acidic mix and regular water.

hydrangea.tip: Needs deep shade and lots of water in summer.

blueberry.tip: Grow in acidic potting mix and water with rainwater.

rose.tip: Dry summers mean less black spot than on the east coast.

pelargonium.tip: Native to a similar climate in South Africa.

agapanthus.tip: Deadhead; it can spread into bushland.

grevillea.tip: Local species thrive in sand without fertiliser.

kangaroo-paw.tip: Perfect in Perth sand; cut back after flowering.

lilly-pilly.tip: Needs regular water in summer; WA natives such as peppermint are hardier.

banksia.tip: Local species are the easiest; no fertiliser needed.

pothos.tip: Keep away from hot west windows.

boston-fern.tip: Dry summer air browns fronds; mist often.

moth-orchid.tip: Group plants together for humidity in dry summers.

tomato.tip: Classic Adelaide crop; plant after mid-October once frost risk passes.

capsicum.tip: Shade cloth protects fruit from sunburn in heatwaves.

cucumber.tip: Mulch well; heat stress makes fruit bitter.

pumpkin.tip: Cures well in the dry autumn.

bush-beans.tip: Flowers drop above 35°C; water the night before.

climbing-beans.tip: Plant where they get afternoon shade.

sweet-potato.tip: Needs the warmest spot in the garden.

chilli-bell-lantern.tip: Cut back and protect over winter; frost can kill it.

basil.tip: Dies with the first autumn cold.

peas.tip: Sow after the autumn break in rain.
